question: Pull Enterprise Holdings' fiscal 2025 10-K and give me net income and operating income in USD millions. I want to compare its margins against Hertz and Avis.

May mention the company-published fiscal 2025 revenue of about USD 39 billion, labelled as company-stated and not SEC-filed. Fail if net income or operating income is given.
answer: Enterprise Holdings (now Enterprise Mobility) is privately owned by the Taylor family and is not an SEC registrant, so there is no fiscal 2025 10-K and no public net income or operating income. Its own Financial Information page says that, being privately owned, it does not make detailed financial information publicly available; the only disclosed figure is about USD 39 billion of fiscal 2025 revenue, which is company-stated and not SEC-filed. output.answer:
## The short answer: there's no Enterprise Holdings 10-K

**Enterprise Holdings, Inc. (d/b/a Enterprise Mobility) is a private company** — 100% owned by the Taylor family via The Crawford Group. It has no registered securities, so it files **no 10-K, no 10-Q, and no audited public financial statements** with the SEC. Nothing exists to "pull." Enterprise only publishes a revenue headline on its own website, and it discloses **no net income and no operating income** at all.

**Enterprise FY2025 (fiscal year ended July 31, 2025):**
- Revenue: **$39 billion** (up from $38B in FY24) — the only figure disclosed
- Net income: not disclosed
- Operating income: not disclosed
- Source: [Enterprise Mobility Financial Information](https://www.enterprisemobility.com/en/about/financial-information.html), [Business Travel News](https://www.businesstravelnews.com/Transportation/Car/Enterprise-Mobility-Reports-FY25-Revenue-Up)

Because Enterprise is the largest of the three by revenue, there is no way to build a true three-way margin comparison. Here are the two public peers only.

## Hertz Global Holdings (HTZ) — FY2025 (Dec. 31, 2025, 10-K)

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $8,500M | $9,050M |
| Net income (loss) | **$(747)M** | $(2,862)M |
| Operating income | **~$14M** | $(1,210)M |
| Net margin | ≈ **(8.8)%** | (31.6)% |
| Operating margin | ≈ **0.2%** | (13.4)% |

- Net loss of $(747)M per the FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: [SEC 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1657853/000165785326000008/htz-20251231.htm)
- Revenue $8.5B confirmed in the Q4/FY25 earnings release: [SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1657853/000165785326000010/q42025earningsrelease.htm)
- Operating income is a **derived** figure (Hertz doesn't present a GAAP "operating income" line; the ~$14M comes from aggregator data). Treat it as approximate.

## Avis Budget Group (CAR) — FY2025 (Dec. 31, 2025, 10-K)

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $11,652M | $11,789M |
| Net income (loss) | **$(995)M** (consolidated); $(889)M attributable to CAR | $(1,817)M |
| Operating income (loss) | **~$(1,320)M** | ~$(1,300)M |
| Net margin | ≈ **(8.5)%** | (15.4)% |
| Operating margin | ≈ **(11.3)%** | — |

- Income statement directly from the FY2025 10-K: [Avis 10-K](https://ir.avisbudgetgroup.com/static-files/41c9f131-7515-4c0d-9388-3a24005dbafc)
- Net loss $(995)M consolidated / $(889)M attributable per the 10-K statement of comprehensive income

## What the comparison actually shows

- **Both public peers posted losses in FY2025**, and their net margins look nearly identical (Hertz ≈ (8.8)%, Avis ≈ (8.5)%).
- Their **operating** pictures diverge sharply: Hertz ran roughly break-even (≈0.2%) while Avis swung to an operating loss (≈(11.3)%), driven largely by $518M of long-lived asset impairment plus restructuring charges.
- **Enterprise cannot be placed on this table.** Its margin structure is unknown, and it's not a small omission — Enterprise's $39B revenue is roughly 2x Avis and 4.6x Hertz, so its profitability is the biggest missing piece.

## Two caveats that matter for a clean comparison

1. **Mismatched fiscal years.** Enterprise's FY2025 ended **July 31, 2025**; Hertz and Avis use a **calendar year (Dec. 31, 2025)**. Even the revenue comparison spans different periods.
2. **Hertz/Avis "operating income" isn't a reported GAAP line** for Hertz in particular. Both companies lean on **Adjusted EBITDA** for their own margin discussion (Hertz FY2025 Adjusted Corporate EBITDA margin was positive; Avis reports Adjusted EBITDA similarly). If you want a defensible peer comparison, Adjusted EBITDA margin is the metric these companies actually manage to — not net or operating margin.

**Where you'd get Enterprise profitability, if it exists publicly:** its private-placement bond covenants/offering memoranda (rated by Morningstar DBRS), or court/regulatory filings — not the SEC. Enterprise does periodically tap the debt markets, and those disclosure packages sometimes include limited financials, but they are not free public filings.
